due_when.clears_when: open_pr_record.py reports the two populations SEPARATELY and its completeness verdict is reachable — i.e. a manager that has recorded every human/session-authored open PR can obtain a verdict other than `unrecorded`, while the automation count stays VISIBLE rather than excluded. ⚠️ SUPPRESSING THE AUTOMATED PRs ENTIRELY DOES NOT RESOLVE THIS AND IS THE WRONG FIX: an automated PR that STOPS self-landing is a real finding, and a filter that hides it converts this noise problem into a silence problem. ⚠️ NOR DOES A GREEN SELF-TEST: the tool's harness cannot reach a live open-PR list, which is the whole input in question. The observation wanted is a real reconcile against a real census producing a verdict a reader can act on. ⚠️ AND IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES the automated PRs SHOULD each carry a hand row, this does not clear — it CHANGES: that is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one rather than left looking like a filter about to be written.

what: [health] ⚠️ NOT A DUPLICATE AND NOT A RECURRENCE — the filing helper flagged 4 lexical neighbours at overlap 0.69 (BL-20260830-A-TRANSIENT-RED-BASE-PERMANENTLY-STRANDS-AN-AUTOMERGE-BRANCH, BL-20260903-PR-OPENER-DRAFT-FALSE-IS-UNREACHABLE-SO-TIER-1-CAN-NEVER-SELF-LAND-THROUGH-THE-RELAY, BL-20260907-COORDINATION-BOARD-6927-IS-FULL-SO-THE-MANDATORY-START-POST-IS-IMPOSSIBLE-BY-EVERY-PATH, BL-20260911-REPLAY-PREGATE-NIGHTLY-HAS-ZERO-SUCCESSFUL-RUNS-IN-ITS-ENTIRE-LIFE-AND-25-MONTHS-OF-ML-PREGATE-EVIDENCE-HAS-ACCRUED-TO-NOTHING) and all four were READ before re-filing. They share this row's vocabulary (PR, auto-merge, self-land, automation) and none is about open_pr_record.py or about a completeness metric; the overlap is the helper's stated LEXICAL measure doing its job, not a prior filing of this defect. THE DEFECT: scripts/ops/open_pr_record.py grades OPEN-PRS.json's completeness against EVERY open PR and makes no automated/human distinction, so 68 self-landing `chore(...)(auto)` PRs opened by scheduled workflows count against a HAND-MAINTAINED handoff record. MEASURED 2026-09-19 over a full census (all 82 open PRs, the UNION of both pages of list_pull_requests(state=open, perPage=50); page 2 returned 32 < 50, so this is a census and not a page): 82 open, 14 recorded after a reconcile that added all 6 missing human-authored PRs, 68 unrecorded and ALL 68 automated. The verdict therefore reads `completeness=unrecorded` whether the manager reconciled diligently or did nothing at all — the two are indistinguishable from the output, which is the desensitised-alarm P1 this repo names as its own worst failure mode, inside the very tool built to make a handoff honest. ⚠️ THE COST IS NOT COSMETIC: it hid a real row. #12497 is a Tier-2 `landing: hold` PR awaiting ONE operator OK since 2026-09-18 with mergeable_state `clean`; it had NO row in OPEN-PRS.json and was carried ONLY by an hourly check-in routine that had fired 33 times — and a routine cannot supply an operator decision, so every firing was noise about a condition it could never clear. A permanently-red completeness verdict is exactly what makes a genuinely-missing row invisible. ⚠️ THE FIX IS NOT SIMPLY 'EXCLUDE chore('. Matching on a title prefix is a string with no denominator behind it (UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class B), and an automation that changed its title would silently leave the population. Partition on something structural — the opening actor, or a self-landing branch namespace such as automation/** — and REPORT both counts separately rather than dropping one: `unrecorded (human)` and `unrecorded (automation)` are different facts, and collapsing them is how this started.
